main_body: Stove: a grey-blue metal body with a light top plate (rows 9-12) and a large front panel (rows 14-29) holding a recessed fire opening with flames
top_band: light blue-grey plate rows 9-12 (L170-215), with a dark outline at row 8 and a dark line at row 13, then the front face
evidence: Column x=8 reads: outline row 8, a light band rows 9-11 with a brighter edge at row 12, a dark line at row 13, then a mid-grey front face rows 14-29 holding a dark firebox. The top band is only about 3-4 rows against 16+ rows of face. The light band has two small dark dots and reads more like a flat plate or a front-facing panel than a horizontal surface seen from above. The firebox is a vertical opening painted face-on. Overall it looks like a front elevation with a small hat, similar to the red 'front elevation: top 1' and 'rim only' guide drawings. The top is too thin to read as a surface, and the stove sits straight-on with no foreshortened top depth.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The body is a flat grey-blue panel with barely any grain or tile detail. 60% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is partly near-black sticker style, and the very dark interior (L=19) is a plain flat fill. The flame has a nice 4-step ramp, but the rest of the ramps are shallow, so it looks thinner and flatter than the references.
